comparison: Strong agreement on intact initial learning and retention despite mPFC lesions. Both evaluations accept the null findings across behavioral measures (C7-C8, C24-C27, C32-C33) as valid evidence. OpenEval emphasizes statistical rigor with effect sizes and repeated measures ANOVA, while peer reviewers note the findings are 'solid' despite being primarily null results and provide 'convincing evidence' that these behaviors do not depend on mPFC.

Complete agreement on lesion effectiveness and metabolic changes. Both evaluations accept claims C5-C6, C35-C40, C59 as demonstrating anatomically effective lesions with network-level functional changes. OpenEval highlights the statistical rigor (FDR correction, test of proportions) and convergence of CO activity with electrophysiological evidence. Peer reviewers confirm 'convincing evidence' and note data were 'collected in a rigorous way' with no concerns raised.

Agreement on selective deficit in conflict learning (C9, C28-C31, C34, C62, C83), but peer review extends to theoretical implications (C84-C85, C88-C90) that OpenEval addresses separately. Both accept the dissociation between intact initial learning and impaired conflict learning as evidence for mPFC's specific role in cognitive flexibility. Peer reviewers note the conflict deficit was 'interpreted as a cognitive flexibility deficit rather than a cognitive control failure' and that initial task results were 'somewhat expected.'

Strong agreement on intact hippocampal representational switching and SFEP (C10, C52-C58, C80). Both evaluations accept that cognitive control of spatial information persists without mPFC. OpenEval emphasizes statistical rigor (runs tests, two-way ANOVAs) and appropriate modulation by shock location. Peer reviewers confirm 'convincing evidence' that hippocampal representations 'do not depend on the medial prefrontal cortex' and accept intact SFEP as evidence against mPFC necessity. Peer review also includes overdispersion findings (C48-C51, C63-C64) that OpenEval evaluates separately.

Agreement on overdispersion findings (C48-C51, C63-C64) showing task-dependent changes in discharge reliability. OpenEval notes the nuanced finding of reduced overdispersion during pretraining with normalization during avoidance, suggesting compensatory mechanisms. Peer reviewers accept this as 'the only difference in hippocampal activity' between groups, occurring only during pretraining. Both evaluations support the interpretation that place cell tuning was intact while discharge reliability varied.

Agreement on major theoretical conclusions rejecting central-computation hypothesis (C75, C78, C92), but with important caveats from peer review. OpenEval finds strong support for local-computation based on convergence of behavioral and neural evidence. Peer reviewers largely agree the findings support the local hypothesis and 'will have a significant impact,' but Reviewer 3 raises conceptual concerns about whether the task truly requires cognitive control as defined in broader literature, noting the definition used is 'much simpler' than standard definitions.

Partial overlap on theoretical claims about mPFC's role in selecting between competing memories (C84-C85, C89-C90). OpenEval groups these with broader theoretical conclusions (C75, C78, C92) as supported by the dissociation pattern. Peer review addresses these claims when discussing the conflict learning deficit, accepting the interpretation that mPFC has a specific role in cognitive flexibility and memory selection rather than general cognitive control.

Agreement on thalamic electrophysiology (C65) showing task-dependent changes. OpenEval includes this as part of converging evidence for network-level functional changes from mPFC lesions. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this finding (reported in supplementary data) with no concerns raised, though it was not specifically discussed in reviews.

Agreement on anatomical connectivity and loss of metabolic correlations (C66-C67). OpenEval notes these findings are consistent with known anatomical connectivity and strengthen inference of non-local lesion effects. Peer reviewers accept the correlation findings but note (Reviewer 2) that 'the discussion is lacking any mechanistic interpretations' - a critique of interpretation depth rather than validity of the findings.

Agreement on anatomical knowledge about nucleus reuniens as relay (C68). Both evaluations accept this established anatomical fact with appropriate citations. OpenEval groups this with methodological context (C23, C119), while peer review addresses it alongside metabolic correlation findings (C66-C67).

Agreement on interpretation that conflict impairment demonstrates lesion effectiveness (C88). OpenEval notes this inference is well-supported by behavioral data as part of acknowledging limitations and alternative interpretations. Peer review implicitly accepts this when discussing the dissociation between intact initial learning and impaired conflict learning.

OpenEval evaluates background claims about cognitive control and PFC function from literature (C1-C2, C12-C17) as supported with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - these are established background knowledge that reviewers did not specifically comment on.

OpenEval evaluates prior experimental work establishing the active place avoidance task and hippocampal role (C3-C4, C18-C19, C21, C69-C74, C79, C81) as accurately summarized with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - these are literature-based contextual claims that reviewers did not specifically address.

OpenEval evaluates the articulation of competing hypotheses (C20, C22) as clearly stated and providing testable predictions. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though Reviewer 3's concern about the definition of cognitive control relates indirectly to the hypothesis framing.

OpenEval evaluates methodological background claims about overdispersion and SFEP measures (C41-C47) as accurately described with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - these are established methodological concepts that reviewers did not specifically comment on.

OpenEval evaluates conceptual clarifications (C82, C91) about the distinction between evidence of cognitive control versus cognitive control itself, and hippocampal dependence of memory-guided control. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - reviewers did not specifically address these conceptual distinctions.

OpenEval evaluates comprehensive methodological details (C93-C126) as well-documented with appropriate controls, established techniques, and sufficient detail for replication. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - reviewers accepted the methods without specific commentary on individual procedural claims.
